routes.label: Wilmington to Philadelphia (Thomas Garrett)
routes.source: Foner, "Middle Atlantic", NPS Underground Railroad Handbook (Dickinson, HB-FONER); Wikipedia, "Thomas Garrett" (WP-GARRETT)
routes.note: TEST ROW for the Underground Railroad layer (owner's request of 2026-11-17); not reviewed. Research and full citations: docs/UNDERGROUND-RAILROAD.md. Garrett worked in Wilmington from 1822 and sent people on to the Philadelphia committee. 1861: J. Miller McKim's remark that the Underground Railroad was in effect over (HB-FONER); the NPS itself runs it to 1865. Last documented 1861; no source records an end, so the row holds it open to 1865, the NPS's end for the Underground Railroad. Places, in order: Wilmington, Philadelphia.

routes.label: Eastern Shore of Maryland to Wilmington (Harriet Tubman's route)
routes.source: NPS, Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad NHP, "Harriet Tubman" (NPS-TUB); Wikipedia, "Harriet Tubman", citing Larson 2004 and Clinton 2004 (WP-TUB)
routes.note: TEST ROW for the Underground Railroad layer (owner's request of 2026-11-17); not reviewed. Research and full citations: docs/UNDERGROUND-RAILROAD.md. Poplar Neck near Preston, then Sandtown, Camden (the Brinkleys and Abraham Gibbs), past Dover and Smyrna, New Castle, Wilmington (Garrett), Philadelphia (William Still). Her own escape, autumn 1849; return trips 1850 to 1860. This is the chain of her later trips as Larson reconstructs it: the way of her first escape is not known. East New Market (Sam Green) and Willow Grove are on the chain in the source and left off the line, which is too short to show them apart. Last documented 1860; no source records an end, so the row holds it open to 1865, the NPS's end for the Underground Railroad. Places, in order: Preston, Sandtown, Camden, Dover, Smyrna, New Castle, Wilmington, Philadelphia.

routes.label: Philadelphia to New York
routes.source: Foner, "Middle Atlantic" (HB-FONER); NPS handbook timeline (HB-TIME)
routes.note: TEST ROW for the Underground Railroad layer (owner's request of 2026-11-17); not reviewed. Research and full citations: docs/UNDERGROUND-RAILROAD.md. 1835: David Ruggles founds the New York Committee of Vigilance. By train and ferry across New Jersey; no source read names a New Jersey town except Siebert (1898), from recollections. Last documented 1861; no source records an end, so the row holds it open to 1865, the NPS's end for the Underground Railroad. Places, in order: Philadelphia, New York.

routes.label: New York to Canada by Albany, Syracuse and Niagara
routes.source: Foner, "Middle Atlantic" (HB-FONER); Harrold, "Washington, Maryland, Virginia" (HB-HARROLD); NPS theme study, 2000 (NPS-THEME)
routes.note: TEST ROW for the Underground Railroad layer (owner's request of 2026-11-17); not reviewed. Research and full citations: docs/UNDERGROUND-RAILROAD.md. Albany (Stephen Myers), Syracuse (Jermain Loguen), Rochester (Frederick Douglass), Buffalo, the Niagara crossing, St. Catharines. 1842: Charles Torrey's party reaches Albany, the earliest dated use of the road north of New York in what was read; Sydney Howard Gay's record of 1855 to 1856 documents Syracuse best. The Albany leg is less fully attested than the Syracuse leg. Last documented 1861; no source records an end, so the row holds it open to 1865, the NPS's end for the Underground Railroad. Places, in order: New York, Albany, Syracuse, Rochester, Buffalo, Niagara Falls, St. Catharines.
